messages.subject: Stagnant sampler problem.
parts:
Hi,

I have coded up a two-layer hierarchical model using the newest software on Windows (newest R, newest Stan).

Stan appears to be sampling on screen but when I ask to print the results, there does not appear to be any variation in the posterior distribution. I.e., the sampler just reports the same values for all percentiles like this:

Inference for Stan model: storechoice_fullparam.
1 chains, each with iter=100; warmup=50; thin=1; 
post-warmup draws per chain=50, total post-warmup draws=50.

theta[2]           -1.04    0.00   0.0     -1.04     -1.04     -1.04     -1.04     -1.04     6 1.30
lambda[1]           2.62    0.00   0.0      2.62      2.62      2.62      2.62      2.62     3 2.07
lambda[2]           6.28    0.00   0.0      6.28      6.28      6.28      6.28      6.28     4 1.71
betainbar[1]       -1.39    0.00   0.0     -1.39     -1.39     -1.39     -1.39     -1.39     4 1.36
betainbar[2]       -1.62    0.00   0.0     -1.62     -1.62     -1.62     -1.62     -1.62     3 1.81



This happens when I submit my own initial values or when I let the sampler to initialize. When I ask for an output of log-likelihood, it looks like this:
here is log-20302.2

here is log-16448.5

here is log-16602.5

here is log-16448.5

here is log-16467.6

here is log-16448.5

here is log-16452.2

here is log-16448.5

here is log-16449.4

here is log-16448.5


So very few variation. There also a few errors but not too many (around 8-9).

Could you please give me some general advice on how to debug or approach this problem? I can also add the code if is helpful.

messages.author: 1c70f0703f55d650
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stagnant sampler problem.
parts:
Thanks for taking a look!
The data enters through the likelihood. Some background: In the model all consumers get individual level coefficients from population level distributions and make purchasing decisions. Likelihood for the quantity bought is somewhat complex but depends on things like prices and individual level coefficients.

The likelihood is basically gumbel_pdf(Va/sigmaeps) for quantities that were purchased and gumbel_cdf(Va/sigmaeps) for quantites that were not purchased, where Va is an expression that depends on data and individual level coefficients. In addition, there is the Jacobian.

I will double check everything but as it currently is, data should be playing a role.

at it. Is there any way to start with a simpler model and
build up to something like this?

Your model hasn't converged. All R-hat values should be near 1.

Was that output from multiple diffuse random inits? That is,
do all the chains go to the same fixed values? Can you see
them moving there during warmup if you plot warmup draws?
